about.text: A Namibian soured buttermilk, acidified by women and eaten with maize porridge, mainly among the Herero, Himba and Mbanderu in the Kunene, Omaheke and Otjozondjupa regions; it is also mass-produced in Namibia and made in Botswana. Omashikwa, the Ovambo and Herero version, is made by fermenting milk for two or three days with omunkunzi root and a starter, then hand-churning out the butter.
